about.text: The Sikh Student Association is a club where Sikh and Panjabi students can build a community amongst students of a similar background. The goals of this organization is to uphold the three pillars of Sikhi which include: Vand Shakna (sharing with others), Kirat Karni (Honest Living), and Naam Japna (Praying/meditation). This club will create awareness of the presence of Sikh/Panjabi students on campus, teach others about the core principles of our beliefs, and share parts of our culture such as food, music, and history with the greater student population.

about.text: The Sikh Student Association at California State University, Fullerton, is built to create a welcoming environment for Sikh students to foster educational dialogue about the Sikh faith and its practices. about.text: The Sikh Student Association at CSULB is dedicated to fostering a vibrant, inclusive community at California State University, Long Beach, that embodies the core Sikh values of Kirat Karni (honest living), Vand Chakna (sharing with others), and Naam Japna (focus on God). Our mission is to promote the understanding and appreciation of Sikh culture, heritage, and principles through educational, cultural, and social initiatives. We strive to provide a supportive and nurturing environment where students can explore and celebrate Sikh heritage, culture, and values and encourage personal growth, community service, and intercultural dialogue.

about.text: CWRU's Sikh Student Association is a student-based religious organization that will raise awareness of Sikhism across campus while practicing community outreach, equality, and interfaith dialogue. This will be accomplished through service projects in the Cleveland area as well as at the local Sikh temples. There will also be guest speakers and informational meetings to educate students on current issues that Sikhs across the world face as well as fundraising opportunities to aid them. This club will work to create a safe community for Sikh and non-Sikh students that want to learn about Sikhism, connect with others, and help their community.

about.text: The Sikh Student Association at George Mason University welcomes everyone! George Mason University's Sikh Student Association was established in 2007. The organization was created as a platform for Sikh students to come together and get involved in the community and live up to the principles of Sikhism. about.text: The Sikh Student Association at Stanford (SSA) is a tight-knit family and we are delighted to welcome you into our community. Our organization serves as a space to congregate, explore and engage with Sikhi. We also strive to broaden the understanding and awareness of the Sikh religion and heritage in the Stanford community through cultural, cross-cultural, social, religious, and political activities. Our members come from various backgrounds and contribute their unique insights and experiences to better our collective understanding and experience with Sikhi. In the past, we have hosted events ranging from a discussion series on civic engagement within the Sikh community, inviting Sikh professionals in the community to speak with our group, and most recently, a panel on the Kisan Morcha.
about.sourceLabel: Stanford's Office for Religious & Spiritual Life

about.text: The Sikh Students’ Association of UBC was established in 1985 and is a way for students at UBC to connect with each other and with Sikhi while making impactful contributions to the greater Lower Mainland community. As a club, we hope to make learning about and experiencing Sikhi more accessible to university students and foster a positive community for Sikh students. about.text: The Sikh Student Association is an organization at the University of California, Davis that provides students with an environment that allows for a greater exploration of Sikhi. Through hosting Kirtan Nights, Discussions, Socials, Seva (selfless service), Peer Mentoring, and Professional Development Opportunities, we incorporate the three main tenets of Sikhi: Naam Japo (Remembrance of God), Kirat Karo (Honest Work), and Vand Chhako (Sharing With Others). In doing so, we strive to advance the academic and spiritual pursuits of students at UC Davis, as well as build an inclusive and supportive community that serves all.
